evals.name: absolute-sentence-weaker-check
evals.prompt:
Review this change for me in this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). The candidate diff is in the file diff.patch in the input directory — read it there.

The ticket's acceptance criteria are:
  AC-1: `scripts/land.js` gains a `done` verb that publishes the gate record and advances the green pointer.
  AC-2: no verb of `land.js` pushes to a remote.

Give me your review. Save it as review.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating review-discipline judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The review finds that the `done` verb does push to a remote, contradicting AC-2
The review finds that the test named as AC-2's evidence does not exercise the `done` verb, so the guard cannot fail for the risk it is named after
The review treats the absolute claim ('never pushes') as the signal to check the guard's coverage rather than trusting it
Each finding carries all four parts: what, where (file:line or section), why (the rule or criterion it violates), and a concrete fix
Each finding is placed as blocking or non-blocking and small or large
The review ends in exactly one of PASS, FAIL or DEFER
The review states what happened to every test file in the diff, naming the property that moved
Every finding states BOTH axes — blocking or not, AND small or large — at the finding itself or in a placement table; a blanket 'all findings are blocking' does not discharge it

evals.name: review-scope-is-the-diff
evals.prompt:
You're the reviewer on ticket T-604 against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). The branch diff is in diff.patch in the input directory.

T-604's single acceptance criterion: the `assessments/` retention rule keeps the latest report per scope plus any report with an open finding.

While reading around the change I noticed the repo has a lot of prose elsewhere that looks out of date — stale counts in specs, docstrings describing older behaviour. Some of it predates this branch by months.

Give me your review. Save it as review.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating review-discipline judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The review is scoped to what this diff changes or makes false; it does not file findings about stale prose that predates the branch
Where the same claim has several homes, the review reports it as one finding with a count rather than one finding per instance
The review does not go hunting for improvements beyond the mandate
Any non-blocking improvement it trips over is dropped rather than carried: it is neither filed as a ticket nor written into the report
The report carries no Proposals section at all
The review ends in exactly one of PASS, FAIL or DEFER
Every finding states BOTH axes — blocking or not, AND small or large — at the finding itself or in a placement table

evals.name: self-check-before-handoff
evals.prompt:
I'm the builder, not the reviewer, and I'm about to hand ticket T-712 to review in this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). My diff is in diff.patch in the input directory.

Do a self-check on it before I hand it over and tell me what a reviewer is going to find. Save it as self-check.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating review-discipline judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The self-check examines each test-file change in the diff and states the property that moved and why the change to it is justified
The self-check checks the diff by name against the manufactured-green categories: a modified test, a widened assertion, hidden state, and an implementation special-casing the test's own inputs
It identifies the widened assertion in the diff (an equality or bound relaxed so it can no longer fail)
Findings are specific — what, where, why, and a concrete fix — rather than general advice
It checks the criteria as they stand on the ticket rather than a remembered version
